Review date: 2026-10-02. Active chapter: a_recurrence, Week 2 Algorithms. This is a bounded comparison of eight university candidates; it does not certify discovery of every worldwide course or a globally optimal ranking. Chapter-specific selection considers usable text, proof detail, domain precision, complementary coverage, and useful exercise types.

Reconciled scientific and presentation issues

  1. Stanford's polynomial-toll theorem gives upper conclusions; no tight conclusion is inferred without a lower toll/base or compulsory-work assumption.
  2. MIT's critical log-power case states nonnegative log exponents. The negative-exponent thresholds are derived independently by reversing depth and proving the power-sum estimates.
  3. Cornell Lecture 20's uneven tree illustrates children n/3 and 2n/3, although one displayed equation writes T(n/3)+2T(n/3). The new lesson states the intended unequal model explicitly and distinguishes the two trees.
  4. Cornell Recitation 19's larger envelope is written with original T children in the last display. The lesson defines envelopes recursively on themselves and proves comparison. The reciprocal-log recurrence is solved tightly rather than merely bounded by n log n.
  5. CMU's shrinking-mass theorem is displayed after an upper inequality with a theta conclusion. The chapter separates the proven upper bound from a lower bound supplied by exact positive linear work.
  6. Princeton's size toll and a size-minus-one comparison toll differ by one per internal merge. The exact balanced-tree identity derives both values and explains their equal leading order.
  7. Leighton's polynomial-interval comparability is adopted as an explicit assumption. The remark about a polynomial derivative bound alone is not adopted: a nonnegative smooth function such as sine squared can have zeros and violate the displayed multiplicative comparability condition. Initial logarithmic singularities are handled by a fixed cutoff and bounded extension.
  8. The full perturbation proof in later Leighton pages was not read or reproduced. The lesson proves the unperturbed theorem, handles selected floors/ceilings independently, and does not apply a general perturbation theorem to arbitrary child arguments.
  9. Tree identities retain positive base work and distinguish internal levels from leaves. Mathematical weighted recurrences are distinguished from physical recursive-call counts.

Individual revision, 13 October 2026

The historical comparison above is supplemented by fresh actual reading of five independent written university scopes: all seven pages of MIT 6.006 Spring 2020 Recitation 3; all six pages of Stanford CS161 Lecture 3, whose actual header identifies Winter 2026, plus the complete one-page solved concept check; CMU 15-451 Fall 2011 physical pages 10–15 and selected pages 24–26; the entire available Princeton Analysis of Algorithms Chapter 2 webpage, including its selected exercises; and both complete Cornell recursion-tree and substitution pages. All nine pages of Tom Leighton's MIT supplement were read, with physical pages two and three also rendered and visually inspected. The exact reading ledger separates successful direct acquisitions from CMU's failed direct fetch and successful official-browser reading. The eight-candidate pool is bounded; Berkeley, Oxford and ETH are screened candidates, not claimed as newly read complete courses.

The entire retained lesson, all forty derivation tutorials, all eighty earlier review rules and all fifty-three canonical question stems/options were read before authoring. All fifty-three answers are independently rewritten with exact substitutions, seed checks, matching lower bounds where needed, original-variable restoration and individual option diagnoses. The answer manuscript contains 11,173 words; length is an observed property, not a quality guarantee. Eight deeper constructions, ten fully solved transfer challenges, a complete ten-point mathematical summary and forty detailed examination decisions supplement the full lesson. Original and course-informed challenges are independently worded and do not claim to reproduce all university exercise collections.

Seven authentic examination items were actually visually reread and their unchanged original PDF hashes checked. An enlarged original MS CE 1405 Q58 crop revealed wrong canonical options two, three and four. The printed alternatives are O(log n log log n), O(n log n log log n), O(n log log n) and O(log log n). The first is tightest; the next two are also true upper bounds. The canonical producer, recurrence chapter and earlier asymptotic chapter are corrected, and the literal wording ambiguity remains visible. No certified official answer key is claimed. The sampled-pivot question explicitly distinguishes an allowed extreme-split abstraction from a simultaneously realizable worst-case proof.

Source mathematical qualifications are independently reconciled. Leighton's critical reciprocal-log example must multiply by log log x rather than divide, and the lower constant must use the lower toll bound. A bounded derivative alone does not guarantee multiplicative comparability. Cornell's unequal equation and intended tree disagree; its comparison envelope must recur on itself. MIT and Stanford upper formulations do not automatically supply tight lower work. Princeton size-toll merging is distinct from comparison toll size minus one. Negative logarithmic thresholds, concrete floor-square-root errors, uniform-pivot conditioning and integer stopping rules are derived explicitly.

Forty-six dedicated models contain 324 unique checkpoints, including exact complete level aggregates, prefix ledgers, modular pair cycles, full rounded merge trees, repeated-root normalization, multiplicative exponent ledgers, slowly shrinking integer chains, memoized dependencies and full discrete rank distributions. Illustrative fragments are labeled and never represented as the complete tree. The final source has sixty-seven actual players, seventy-seven scenario placements and 542 mounted checkpoints. A separate final pass checks 517 mounted new or repaired-tree frames after typography and color repairs. All 402 control operations, 134 actual play/pause assertions, twenty scenario selections, six recurrence laboratory records, five static figures, three widths and print passed. Eight static directed edges are clipped to their circle ports with resolved small markers. Prose, mathematics and code retain separate fonts; named function spacing is repaired without changing any tutorial's mathematical content.

Independent checks evaluate 57,113 assertions, including exact recurrence iterations, 1,999 integer rounded-merge inputs, 9,999 slowly shrinking inputs, square-root transformed bounds and 499 actual uniform-rank distributions. Seventeen fully numeric printed end-equalities are evaluated separately. These finite oracles supplement the explicit general proofs; they do not certify arbitrary nonlinear recurrences or unseen exam performance. The rewritten edition remains a checked review draft. The standing user authorization permits continued work on a_divide in the frozen order, while unfinished l_projection authoring is preserved.
